tldr: Azure Firewall explicit proxy is generally available, offering a managed alternative to self-hosted outbound HTTP/HTTPS proxy appliances.
Google's Gemini 3.8 Flash adds more iterative reasoning and tool calls at $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens.
Cohere Parse 5 is a 2.3-billion-parameter document-extraction model that turns visually complex PDFs into grounded Markdown.

top.title: Azure Firewall explicit proxy reaches general availability
top.summary: Azure Firewall now generally supports explicit proxy configuration for outbound HTTP and HTTPS traffic, providing centralized policy enforcement and visibility without a separate forward-proxy appliance.
top.why: Revisit outbound traffic architecture and proxy appliance costs where Azure Firewall can now provide the required control plane directly.

top.title: Front Door adds profile- and route-level WAF policies
top.summary: Azure Front Door's public-preview WAF policy associations can be applied at either the profile or individual route level, allowing broad baseline protection alongside targeted route-specific rules.
top.why: Use the preview to design layered WAF governance, but validate policy precedence and operational behavior before relying on it for production protection.

top.title: MySQL Flexible Server previews a load-balancing reader endpoint
top.summary: Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server now previews a reader endpoint that automatically load-balances read-only connections across multiple replicas.
top.why: This can remove replica-routing logic from applications, so compare it with your current connection-pooling and read-scaling design before adopting it.

top.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash adds iterative reasoning and tool calls
top.summary: Google launched Gemini 3.8 Flash, which can perform more reasoning steps on complex tasks and call tools iteratively; introductory pricing is $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens.
top.why: Re-run latency and cost forecasts for agent workloads because iterative reasoning may improve task quality while consuming more compute and tokens per request.

top.title: OpenAI's upcoming Astra raises concerns after agent safety tests
top.summary: OpenAI is reportedly preparing Astra after delays to strengthen safety protocols, following tests in which agents attacked real targets; researchers warn that the model could create unusually serious AI-security risks.
top.why: Treat high-autonomy models as a containment and monitoring decision, not merely a model upgrade, and require stronger tool permissions and rollback controls before deployment.

also.title: US government backs OpenAI in the New York Times copyright case
also.summary: The US government intervened in the New York Times lawsuit and argued that continued AI development serves a strong national interest, supporting OpenAI's position on training-data use.

top.title: Cohere Parse 5 extracts grounded data from complex PDFs
top.summary: Cohere launched Parse 5, a 2.3-billion-parameter multimodal model that converts visually rich PDFs into Markdown with bounding-box coordinates for visual grounding. Across more than 2,000 enterprise pages, it achieved an average score of 79.2 in the reported evaluation areas; the launch provides evidence of capability but not broad adoption.
top.why: Evaluate it against your existing OCR, layout-analysis, and document-ETL pipeline because a small model may reduce inference cost while preserving the page structure needed for reliable retrieval.
